wa_mossness.blurb: Mossness is a ten-route sport wall in the Tyler Peak Crags, on the basalt outcrop above the upper Dungeness River in the Olympics. It forms the nearest rock to the road and is the first wall you meet on the way up through the boulder field. The climbing is steady in the 5.10 and 5.11 range, with a few routes at the easier and harder ends, and the style is crimpy. Tyler Peak sees little traffic and has plenty of encroaching vegetation, so expect a remote, somewhat alpine feel rather than a polished roadside crag.

wa_north_slab.blurb: North Slab is a short friction slab on Mount Erie, on Fidalgo Island, forming the northern half of the Sunset Slab. Ten climbs mix five sport routes, four top-rope lines and one trad route, mostly between 5.4 and 5.8 with one or two harder. Anchors sit at the top, and most routes can be top-roped by walking around to the left, which makes it handy for beginners and instructional groups. Many of the anchors are staples, so extending them cuts down on rope drag.

wa_pend_oreille_county_park.blurb: Pend Oreille County Park holds a compact sport wall tucked among cedars in northeast Washington, just north of the Spokane County line off Highway 2. All ten routes are bolted, and the grades cluster heavily around 5.10, with one easier route near 5.8 or 5.9 and a single 5.11. The wall is shaded and the routes are short, so it suits an afternoon of mileage rather than a big day. The park around it also has trails and a campground.

wi_05_fire_spire.blurb: Fire Spire is a golden sandstone spire on the Pinnacle Wall at Petenwell Rock near Necedah, with a narrow summit and a lone pine on top. It is easy to pick out when approaching from the east. Climbs are split between a river side facing east and a road side facing west. The ten routes are mostly trad with three sport lines, running from about 5.5 up to 5.10, with most in the 5.7 to 5.8 band. Petenwell mixes sport and traditional styles, and the rock quality ranges from hard patina to soft in places.

wi_bulbous.blurb: Bulbous is a small bouldering zone at Devil's Lake, on the Balanced Rock Trail side of the East Bluff. A short cliffline just east of the top of the trail has a boulder below it, and the ten problems range from a beginner-level warm-up through the V2 and V3 middle ground to a handful of serious V5 to V9 lines. Wednesday Nighter is a favorite entry-level problem. You reach it by hiking to the top of the Balanced Rock trail and then picking up a social trail east through the talus.

wi_storm_wrack_wall.blurb: Storm Wrack Wall is a short wall in the woods of Steinke Basin at Devil's Lake, west of Steinke Wall. It has ten climbs: seven trad or top-rope routes from easy fifth class up to about 5.8, plus three boulder problems from V2 to V5. The wall is low and the problems are short, so it works well as a stop on a day exploring the basin. Neighboring Steinke Basin rocks tend toward highball bouldering, and GPS helps for finding the walls from the East Bluff Woods trail.
